questions.prompt: A rolling deploy adds a required field that old services cannot parse.
questions.explanation: Make schema changes backward and forward compatible. In DDIA: Encoding and Evolution, the first move is to protect the system's real guarantee: evolve without breaking old readers.
options: Make schema changes backward and forward compatible
questions.answer: Make schema changes backward and forward compatible

concept_panel.title: Schema Evolution
concept_panel.explanation: Schema evolution is the ability to change stored or transmitted data formats without breaking old readers or writers. Backward compatibility means new code can read old data; forward compatibility means old code can tolerate new data. Rolling upgrades require both versions to coexist. Formats such as JSON are easy to inspect; schema-based formats such as Avro can enforce compatibility through a registry.
key_takeaways: Backward and forward compatibility protect rolling deploys.
Optional fields are safer than new required fields.
Schema registries can block incompatible messages.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand evolvability in long-lived data systems.
concept_panel.practical_example: Add an optional field, deploy readers first, then deploy writers that populate it.
